questions.title: Frequency of the Target
questions.description:
A log analyzer records numeric event codes and needs to know how often a given code shows up. Count the occurrences of target in the array — a hash map such as std::unordered_map turns this into a single pass. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int frequency_of(std::vector<int> v, int target)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the number of times target appears.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Environment Lookup
questions.description:
A deployment tool keeps named settings in an environment map. You get the operation log as parallel arrays: names[i] with values[i] = -1 means UNSET names[i] (erasing a missing name is a no-op); any other values[i] (always >= 0) means SET names[i] = values[i], inserting or overwriting. The final operation reads GET target. Return the current value of target, or -1 when it is unset or was never set. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int env_get(std::vector<std::string> names, std::vector<int> values, std::string target)

Input Format:
Line 1: m (number of ops). Then m op lines: "SET name value", "UNSET name" or "GET name" (exactly one GET, last).

Output Format:
One line with target's value, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 1000, SET values >= 0, names are single words

3
SET timeout 30
SET retries 3
GET retries
questions.input1:
5
SET a 1
SET b 2
SET a 9
UNSET b
GET a
questions.input2:
4
SET x 5
UNSET x
SET x 6
GET x
questions.input3:
3
SET port 8080
UNSET port
GET port
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= m <= 1000, SET values >= 0, names are single words
